strings.name: Bong Joon-ho
strings.role: Film director and screenwriter · Genre cinema and social observation
strings.summary: Bong combines crime, monster films, science fiction and dark comedy with South Korean social experience. From Memories of Murder and The Host to Snowpiercer, he examines institutions, class and ordinary lives. Parasite won the Palme d’Or and the Oscar for Best Picture, expanding Korean-language cinema’s global reach. His filmmaking relies on collaboration with writers, actors and production teams and has extended into English-language films and animation projects.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Released films are covered through Mickey 17 in 2025, alongside the animation plans announced in 2026. The planned 2027 release is not treated as completed.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-01.value: Sociology at Yonsei University; Korean Academy of Film Arts
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Selected films
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Memories of Murder; The Host; Snowpiercer; Parasite
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Parasite’s international breakthrough
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: The film won the 2019 Palme d’Or and the 2020 Oscars for Best Picture, Directing, Original Screenplay and International Feature Film.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Social observation through genre
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Uses crime, monster and science-fiction narratives to examine class and institutions, connecting Korean experiences with international cinematic forms.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: International production
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: From Snowpiercer and Okja to Mickey 17, collaborations with multinational casts and crews have extended his subjects and audiences.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Ally’s release plans announced
strings.timeline.event-01.text: The production company announced a July 2027 Korean release for the animated feature. At the cutoff, this remained a future plan, not a released film.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Releases Mickey 17
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Wrote and directed the science-fiction film starring Robert Pattinson and presented it at the Berlin International Film Festival.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Parasite wins four Oscars
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The film won Best Picture, Directing, Original Screenplay and International Feature Film. Bong shared the screenplay credit with Han Jin-won.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Parasite wins the Palme d’Or
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Used the relationship between wealthy and poor families for a dark comedy and social thriller, winning Cannes’ top award.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Releases Okja
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Built an international story around a girl and a giant animal, continuing his examination of industry and everyday ethics.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Releases Snowpiercer
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Used a train’s hierarchical order for a science-fiction narrative, expanding his work with international actors and English-language production.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Releases The Host
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Combined a monster film with family, environmental and institutional questions, marking an important stage in his international recognition.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Releases Memories of Murder
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Used a serial-crime investigation to examine policing and society, establishing a blend of crime narrative and social observation.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Makes his first feature, Barking Dogs Never Bite
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Began his feature-directing career with an absurd story of apartment life, developing dark humour and stories of ordinary people.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in South Korea
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Later studied sociology and attended the Korean Academy of Film Arts, moving from shorts and screenwriting toward feature filmmaking.
